Tracing observability is adjacent to OS instrumentation but no official repo was found and the technique may depend on hardware tracing, which is blocked here.
Learned cardinality estimator is a query-optimizer component (anchor case), cheap to run single-node CPU with a linked repo.
Tensor-program optimizer with a released AE artifact runs on one Ampere GPU; ML compiler work is systems-adjacent and absolute speedups will shift on consumer silicon.

Offline C++/SAT checker over recorded histories runs perfectly on this box and the encoding/solver is an attackable performance target, but consistency checking is verification tooling rather than OS resource management.

CPU-only single-machine graph runtime with a Zenodo artifact; the traversal-alignment heuristics are a clean improvement target, though graph processing is systems-adjacent.
Cache disaggregation across storage replicas is a real caching-policy topic and replicas can be co-located processes, but the cross-replica network effects that motivate it are lost on one host.
Relational GNN IR and CUDA code generator is ML-compiler work far from OS resource management, though single-GPU evaluation fits.
The paper's own platform (one multicore CPU plus one GPU) matches this machine and the schedule space invites add-ons, but it is an ML compiler and needs a user-space LLVM/MLIR build.
Cost-model-driven CPU-GPU execution planning for GNN training is systems-adjacent and single-node, but the note gives no evidence of artifact completeness.
ILP-based kernel orchestration scales down directly from V100/A100 to the A5000, but it is DNN compiler optimization and the ILP solver dependency plus artifact completeness are unknown.
Single-GPU sparse-conv engine with small datasets runs as-is, and re-autotuning tile sizes for Ampere is itself a testable improvement hypothesis; kernel-level ML work is systems-adjacent.

Buffer-manager page replacement is a textbook OS caching problem, pure user-space C++ on local NVMe in a mature LeanStore branch, and replacement policies are the easiest thing in the world to swap and measure.
Single-node update-in-place KV store using only io_uring/O_DIRECT, C++ user-space build, dataset fits the free disk; RocksDB comparison gives an obvious evaluation frame.
Factorizing ML inference over joins is query-execution work inside Velox; CPU-only and repo linked but far from OS resource management and Velox is a heavy build.
A measurement/reproduction study of GNN systems has limited reusable artifact, and the note says only the lab GitHub org is linked rather than a named repo.
CPU-assisted LoRA adapter serving is ideal topic and hardware fit (7B on one GPU, 16-core CPU assist), but no artifact URL could be found despite the AE badges, which is the blocking risk.

CPU-only analytical and ns-3 simulation modes let a 1k-GPU cluster be studied with zero GPUs and simulator accuracy-vs-speed is a clean hypothesis; the Physical mode must be skipped and the ns-3/MPI build is large.

Harvesting pipeline bubbles is genuine GPU scheduling work and the core mechanism is per-GPU user space, but it needs a two-stage emulation on one A5000 and the Docker-based isolation path must be replaced with cgroup v2 + MPS.
Learning-to-rank query optimizer is the DB-optimizer-ML anchor case; builds and trains fine on one node but is off the OS core.
Inference-context reuse and batching inside a DB engine is interesting batching work but the topic is DB query execution and no repo is linked.
The headline mechanism targets the Hopper Tensor Memory Accelerator which Ampere lacks, so only a subset is exercisable, and the PipeThreader code must be located inside the whole TileLang project.
A scale-up stream engine with its own user-space memory manager and operator scheduler is genuinely OS-flavoured and fits one machine exactly; artifact completeness is unverified.
Verification-plus-training loop is closer to formal methods than resource management, and the Julia/NeuralVerification.jl dependency adds setup cost despite modest hardware needs.
Preemption-aware GPU-cluster scheduling is a good policy topic studyable by simulation, but the paper evaluates a real cluster and the repo has no README, so artifact usability is doubtful.
SLO-aware prefill/decode scheduling already runs Mistral-7B on a single GPU, the closest hardware match in the batch; 24 GB is tight for 7B FP16 plus KV cache and artifact completeness is unknown.
Prefix-cache admission and eviction policy delivered as a trace-driven CPU simulator is the ideal course target: no GPU needed, and policy swaps map straight onto testable hypotheses.
Explicitly a one-GPU-plus-SSD out-of-core system with a tagged EuroSys'23 artifact, so I/O and buffer policies are extendable; graphs must be limited to what 257 GB free allows.

Multi-tier DRAM/SSD prefix-KV placement is exactly OS caching and storage management and is entirely user space, but the released repo is the authors' HyperInfer extension rather than a FAST'25 artifact and only OPT-6.7B fits.
Tensor-level delta compression is a clean CPU-plus-disk storage problem sized for the machine, but no artifact link appears in the preprint.
LSM I/O admission control and deferred compaction is good storage-engine material, but the multi-tenant cloud motivation is hard to recreate and no repo was located.

User-space overload control across single-host root-free services fits the machine and the culprit-scoring policy is a clean improvement target; per-request monitoring may want perf signals that are blocked here.
